_about: KvK readiness checklist and season explainer (/tools/kvk/, F-26). Items with "facts": [] have no card and show "No consensus".

items.text: City Hall 17 to enter the Lost Kingdom.
items.detail: One older guide only; confirm in your kingdom before KvK.

evidence.B01-0503: Entering the Lost Kingdom requires City Hall 17

items.text: Fight your first KvK with T4; treat T5 as a long-term goal.

evidence.A08-0500: For KvK1 the working tier is T4

items.text: If you have T5, keep a T4 reserve: T5 heals cost much more.

evidence.A08-0505: accounts without steady economy should keep fighting with T4 and maintain a T4 reserve

items.text: Field about 3 complete marches, not 5 weak ones.

evidence.A08-0504: ~3 best marches or one complete march are more useful and cheaper to heal

items.text: Keep hospital capacity high and clear it before every fight.
items.detail: Wounded troops beyond capacity die. Use the healing planner for your numbers.

evidence.A08-0502: Wounded troops beyond hospital capacity die

items.text: Know that attacking cities and objectives can kill severely wounded troops outright.

evidence.A08-0502: some actions (attacking cities/objectives) always kill severely wounded

items.text: Arrive with saved speedups, resource items and AP recovery items for KvK healing and scored events.

evidence.A11-0501: save speedups, resources (as items), AP potions for scoring events and KvK healing

items.text: Keep healing speedups apart from your other speedups.
Save AP recovery items for Eve of the Crusade (pre-KvK).

evidence.A09-0007: especially the pre-KvK Eve of the Crusade

items.text: Decide which commander pairs lead your marches and level those, not many.
Build toward one troop type that matches your best commanders.

evidence.A08-0506: Pick one troop type matching your best commanders

items.text: Read your kingdom's KvK requirements before it starts (often a target as a % of your power).
items.detail: Results are compared after KvK, and some kingdoms then publish a migration list.

evidence.B08-0002: Requirements are commonly a DKP (or dead+kill) target proportional to power
evidence.B06-0005: After KvK, leadership publishes who must leave

items.text: Don't engage first: stay behind, retreat early, fill strong rallies and reinforce.

evidence.A08-0503: should not engage first, should stay behind lanes, retreat early, fill strong rallies and reinforce rather than trade alone

items.text: Know your alliance's fight times and how it calls rallies.

explainer.text: A kingdom goes from a Preparation Season to Season 1 (your first KvK), Season 2, Season 3 and then the Season of Conquest, which repeats.
The pre-KvK event, Eve of the Crusade, starts around kingdom day 85–95, and KvK1 around day 100.

evidence.B01-0500: Pre-KvK (Eve of the Crusade) starts around day 85–95 and KvK1 begins around kingdom day 100

explainer.text: The Lost Kingdom is the shared KvK map. Recent reports say Eve of the Crusade now opens together with it.

evidence.B01-0503: the first ~6 days of pre-KvK now overlap the opening of the Lost Kingdom in Season 1 too
evidence.C04-0002: makes Eve of the Crusade open together with the Lost Kingdom

explainer.text: Season 3 is moving from the Light and Darkness story to King of All Britain.

evidence.C04-0007: In 1.1.07 (May 2026) select Season 3 kingdoms started a pioneer of the 'King of All Britain' story in Season 3

explainer.text: After each KvK, results are compared with the kingdom's requirements; low contributors may be asked to migrate.

evidence.B06-0005: After KvK, leadership publishes who must leave

explainer.text: Between seasons, migration follows age limits that were tightened in March 2026.
